messages:
alex.t: Heads-up — seeing ~12-18% slowdown on AWQ int8 weight-only with group_size=64 after the kernel-selector tweak landed. Repro on dedicated and hosted perf lanes. :eyes:
maya.p: ugh, can you paste the numbers? is it tokens/s or p50?
alex.t: quick microbench below (same machine, CUDA 12.1):
```
model=gpt-medium, seq=512, bs=1
old-selector (awq_pack path): tokens/s=1180, p50=40ms
new-selector v2 (chosen path changed): tokens/s=1025, p50=46ms
delta: -13.1% tokens/s, +15% p50
```
cheng.l: did selector choose a different kernel or fall back to generic quant path?
alex.t: logs show it picked awq_generic for many groups. suspect packing/prefetch stride change combined with group_size=64 made tail fraction exceed threshold.
perf-bot: telemetry: kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.959 -> 0.847; avg_pack_bytes: 8192 -> 9216; memcpy_ms_per_forward: 0.9 -> 3.1
sam.k: that memcpy jump screams misaligned buffer or extra pack/unpack hop. any change to pack stride or alignment in the kernel chooser?
alex.t: we changed packing stride from 1 -> 2 to reduce cache pressure in other models. That lowered peak mem footprint but looks like it increased scatter/gather overhead for AWQ weight-only. nvprof snippet: 
```
== NVPROF ==
Memcpy HtoD time increased by ~2.1ms per forward
SM efficiency down 8% on awq paths that hit awq_generic
```
maya.p: could calibration thresholds be different for AWQ vs GPTQ and cause selector to prefer generic awq_generic? I remember a small_tail_fraction threshold was tuned earlier.
cheng.l: yes selector log: 
```
[kernel-chooser] model=gpt, group=64, quant=AWQ, candidate_kernels=[awq_pack64_fast, awq_generic]
selected=awq_generic (reason: small_tail_fraction>0.15)
```
maya.p: small_tail_fraction computed from pack stride and last-group occupancy. If stride=2 we get more half-filled groups -> tail fraction up.
sam.k: two immediate experiments: (A) revert pack stride to 1 and measure; (B) keep stride=2 but increase prefetch buffer / add 256B alignment shim to packing to avoid extra memcpy. Also try group_size sweep 32/64/128.
alex.t: plan: run sweep with these combos. local command I'll run: 
```
./tools/bench_infer --model gpt-medium --quant awq --group 64 --pack-stride 1 --prefetch 2 --iters 1000
```
cheng.l: note KV cache behavior — when pack layout changes we get different cache eviction patterns. I saw evictions/request +0.04 on the failing run. That explains some of the latency variance. Aligning pack buffers to 256B and reducing memcpy should help.
perf-bot: suggestion: add kernel-chooser fallback penalty for awq_generic so fast pack kernels have priority when pack_size_pct>0.75
maya.p: also run with calibration mode toggled: minmax vs quantile-based calibrator. AWQ calibration influences tail quantization and may change which kernel passes accuracy checks. Try `--calib quantile:0.995` vs `--calib minmax`.
sam.k: and compare AWQ vs GPTQ for the same group/pack-stride to see if this is AWQ-specific. If GPTQ doesn't regress, we know it's packing interaction with AWQ group tails.
alex.t: will run three sweeps across dedicated cluster in next hour (pack-stride 1/2, group 32/64/128, calib modes). will post numeric table. If regression persists we should rollback selector v2 for AWQ int8 fast path. :thumbsup:
maya.p: thanks — add perf traces and kernel-chooser logs to the run artifacts. If you can, attach `nvprof --analysis-metrics` output and a tiny pprof CPU flame for the host copy path.
perf-bot: created ticket PERF-2026-328 for tracking (labels: awq,int8,regression,selector-v2).
alex.t: noted. Posting results shortly.
